summary: Christopher I. Beckwith specializes in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, later serving as an editor at Indiana University in 1982.

Christopher Ives is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2000) and became professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2000.

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from the University of Saskatchewan, studied at Kyoto University, and completed his PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn in 2018.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University. He founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy and has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple works in Indology and religious studies. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982), Stony Brook University (attested 1983), and Loyola Marymount University as Doshi Professor (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher Minkowski specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held professorships at Cornell University (1989–2006) and the University of Oxford as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

Christopher Pinney is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He held appointments at the Australian National University (~1990–1993) and Northwestern University (~2004–2005), and became professor of anthropology and visual culture at University College London in 1993.

Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Columbia under Royal W. Weiler, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies in 1972, and was a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. At Harvard University, he served as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and lecturer on the Study of Religion (~1989–2017) and Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (attested 2013).

Christopher Wallis specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from the University of Rochester, University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt, later lecturing at Naropa University.

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Nanking and University of Iowa, teaching English at Nanking (1943–1947), art history at Iowa (~1956–1965), and serving on the faculty at the University of Kansas from 1966.

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at National Central University and Peking University. A co-founder of New Asia College, he taught at National Central University, New Asia Institute, and was the first Chair Professor at CUHK (1963–1974).

Chun-min Yen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Arizona (attested 2004) under Robert M. Gimello and studied with traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.

Chögyam Trungpa was a figure in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology who studied at Oxford and with Dilgo Khyentse. He served at the Young Lamas Home School and founded Kagyu Samye Ling and Naropa University.

Chökyi Gyatso studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khakyab Dorje. He was both a student and teacher of Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and he taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Chökyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology figure. He studied at Rumtek Monastery under the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse, became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976, and founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (attested 2011).

Chüan-ying Yen specializes in history/archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University (attested 1986), where she studied under John M. Rosenfield, Chu-tsing Li, and John Hay.
